questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q3
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: In how many ways can cells in a \( 3 \times 3 \) grid be shaded, such that each row and each column have exactly one shaded cell? An example of one valid shading is shown.
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Elementary Statistics and Probability

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Core Concept(s): Combinatorics, specifically constraints-based permutations (similar to the non-attacking rooks problem).
  • Given: A \(3 \times 3\) grid requiring exactly one shaded cell per row and per column.
  • Find: Total number of valid shading arrangements.

Solution

  • Construct the grid row by row to count the valid permutations.
  • Row 1: Choose any of the 3 columns to place the first shaded cell. → 3 ways
  • Row 2: The shaded cell cannot be placed in the column chosen for Row 1. → 2 remaining columns
  • Row 3: Two columns are already occupied, leaving only 1 available column. → 1 way
  • By the fundamental counting principle: \[3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6\]

Final Answer

Answer: (D) 6

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q4
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
There are 4 red, 5 green, and 6 blue balls inside a box. If \( N \) number of balls are picked simultaneously, what is the smallest value of \( N \) that guarantees there will be at least two balls of the same colour?
One cannot see the colour of the balls until they are picked.
questions.explanation:
Analytical Aptitude → Logic

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Core Concept(s): The Pigeonhole Principle (Worst-case scenario analysis).
  • Given: A box containing 4 red, 5 green, and 6 blue balls. The colors are hidden until picked.
  • Find: The minimum number of balls, \(N\), to guarantee at least two balls share the same color.

Solution

  • To mathematically guarantee an outcome, evaluate the worst-case scenario — the maximum number of picks without satisfying the condition.
  • Worst case: draw exactly 1 red, 1 green, and 1 blue ball → 3 balls drawn, no two the same color.
  • Because there are only 3 colors available, the very next ball (the 4th pick) must match one of the colors already drawn.
  • This 4th ball will inevitably satisfy the condition. Thus, \(N = 4\).

Final Answer

Answer: (A) 4

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q5
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider a circle with its centre at the origin (O), as shown. Two operations are allowed on the circle.
Operation 1: Scale independently along the x and y axes.
Operation 2: Rotation in any direction about the origin.
Which figure among the options can be achieved through a combination of these two operations on the given circle?
questions.explanation:
Spatial Aptitude → Transformation of Shapes

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Core Concept(s): 2D Geometric Transformations (Scaling and Rotation).
  • Given: A circle centered at the origin. Two operations: independent scaling along x/y axes, and rotation about the origin.
  • Find: The resulting figure after applying a combination of these operations.

Solution

  • Operation 1 — Scaling: Scaling a circle independently along the x and y axes (by different factors) transforms it into an ellipse. Because scaling happens relative to the axes, the center of the ellipse remains at the origin.
  • Operation 2 — Rotation: Rotating the ellipse about the origin changes the angle of its major and minor axes, but does not shift the center. It stays anchored at \((0, 0)\).
  • Evaluating the options:
    • Option A: An ellipse centered at the origin but tilted — perfectly matches the transformation chain. ✓
    • Options B and D: Show shapes translated away from the origin. ✗
    • Option C: Is not a complete ellipse. ✗

Final Answer

Answer: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q6
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Elvesland is a country that has peculiar beliefs and practices. They express almost all their emotions by gifting flowers. For instance, if anyone gifts a white flower to someone, then it is always taken to be a declaration of one's love for that person. In a similar manner, the gifting of a yellow flower to someone often means that one is angry with that person.

Based only on the information provided above, which one of the following sets of statement(s) can be logically inferred with certainty?

(i) In Elvesland, one always declares one's love by gifting a white flower.
(ii) In Elvesland, all emotions are declared by gifting flowers.
(iii) In Elvesland, sometimes one expresses one's anger by gifting a flower that is not yellow.
(iv) In Elvesland, sometimes one expresses one's love by gifting a white flower.
questions.explanation:
Analytical Aptitude → Logic

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis / Inference
  • Core Concept(s): Propositional Logic and Reading Comprehension.
  • Given:
    • Elvesland expresses almost all emotions by gifting flowers.
    • Gifting a white flower is always taken as a declaration of love (White \(\rightarrow\) Love).
    • Gifting a yellow flower often means anger.
  • Find: Which statements can be logically inferred with certainty.

Solution

  • (i) "One always declares love by gifting a white flower." — False. The passage establishes (White \(\rightarrow\) Love), but this statement assumes the converse (Love \(\rightarrow\) White), which is not guaranteed.
  • (ii) "All emotions are declared by gifting flowers." — False. The passage explicitly states "almost all" emotions, not all.
  • (iii) "Sometimes anger is expressed with a non-yellow flower." — False. While yellow "often" means anger, there is no textual evidence guaranteeing anger is ever expressed with non-yellow flowers.
  • (iv) "Sometimes one expresses love by gifting a white flower." — True. The passage confirms that gifting a white flower is always taken as a declaration of love; whenever it happens, it expresses love. ✓

Final Answer

Answer: (D) only (iv)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: Three husband-wife pairs are to be seated at a circular table that has six identical chairs. Seating arrangements are defined only by the relative position of the people. How many seating arrangements are possible such that every husband sits next to his wife?
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Elementary Statistics and Probability

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Core Concept(s): Circular Permutations with grouped entities.
  • Given: 3 husband-wife pairs (6 people) seated at a circular table with 6 identical chairs. Constraint: every husband must sit next to his wife.
  • Find: Total number of distinct relative seating arrangements.

Solution

  • Since each husband and wife must sit together, bind each pair into a single unit. We now have 3 distinct units to arrange around the table.
  • Number of ways to arrange \(n\) distinct units in a circle: \[(n-1)! = (3-1)! = 2! = 2 \text{ ways}\]
  • Within each unit, the husband and wife can swap seats: \(2! = 2\) ways per couple.
  • Multiply all independent choices: \[\text{Total} = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 16\]

Final Answer

Answer: (A) 16

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q9
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: If \( x \) satisfies the equation \( 4^{8^x} = 256 \), then \( x \) is equal to _______.
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Numerical Computation and Estimation

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Core Concept(s): Laws of Exponents.
  • Given: The exponential equation \(4^{(8^x)} = 256\).
  • Find: The value of \(x\).

Solution

  • Express both sides using a common base. Since \(256 = 4^4\), substitute: \[4^{(8^x)} = 4^4\]
  • Because the bases are identical, equate the exponents: \[8^x = 4\]
  • Reduce to the prime base 2. Since \(8 = 2^3\) and \(4 = 2^2\): \[(2^3)^x = 2^2 \implies 2^{3x} = 2^2\]
  • Equate the new exponents: \[3x = 2 \implies x = \dfrac{2}{3}\]

Final Answer

Answer: (C) \(\dfrac{2}{3}\)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | GA Q10
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider a spherical globe rotating about an axis passing through its poles. There are three points \( P, Q, \) and \( R \) situated respectively on the equator, the north pole, and midway between the equator and the north pole in the northern hemisphere. Let \( P, Q, \) and \( R \) move with speeds \( v_P, v_Q, \) and \( v_R, \) respectively.
Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Mensuration and Geometry

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Core Concept(s): Circular Motion Dynamics (relationship between linear velocity and radial distance).
  • Given: A spherical globe rotating on its polar axis. Three points: P (equator), Q (north pole), and R (midway between them). Speeds are \(v_P\), \(v_Q\), and \(v_R\).
  • Find: The correct ordering of their linear speeds.

Solution

  • For any rigid body rotating around an axis, the angular velocity \((\omega)\) is exactly the same for all points on the body.
  • The linear speed of any point is given by: \[v = r\omega\] where \(r\) is the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.
  • Point P (Equator): At the maximum distance from the axis (\(r = \text{globe radius}\)). → \(v_P\) is the highest.
  • Point Q (North Pole): Sits precisely on the axis of rotation (\(r = 0\)). → \(v_Q = 0\).
  • Point R (Midway): At 45° latitude, with \(r\) strictly between 0 and the globe's radius. → \(v_R\) is strictly between \(v_Q\) and \(v_P\).
  • Combining: \[v_P > v_R > v_Q\]

Final Answer

Answer: (C) \(v_P > v_R > v_Q\)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Let \( \phi \) be a scalar field, and \( \mathbf{u} \) be a vector field. Which of the following identities is true for \( \text{div}(\phi \mathbf{u}) \)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus — Vector Identities and Operations

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Scalar field \(\Phi\), vector field \(\mathbf{u}\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct vector identity for \( ext{div}(\Phi\mathbf{u})\).

2. Core Concepts:

Key Vector Calculus Identity:\[ abla \cdot (\Phi\mathbf{u}) = \Phi( abla \cdot \mathbf{u}) + \mathbf{u} \cdot ( abla\Phi)\]Or in notation:\[ ext{div}(\Phi\mathbf{u}) = \Phi\cdot ext{div}(\mathbf{u}) + \mathbf{u}\cdot ext{grad}(\Phi)\]

SymbolMeaning
\( abla \cdot \mathbf{u}\)Divergence of vector field \(\mathbf{u}\)
\( abla\Phi\) or \( ext{grad}(\Phi)\)Gradient of scalar field \(\Phi\)
\(\mathbf{u} \cdot abla\Phi\)Dot product (scalar result)

3. Solution Method (Derivation from First Principles):

\[ ext{div}(\Phi\mathbf{u}) = \dfrac{\partial(\Phi u_x)}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial(\Phi u_y)}{\partial y} + \dfrac{\partial(\Phi u_z)}{\partial z}\]Applying product rule to each term:\[= \Phi\dfrac{\partial u_x}{\partial x} + u_x\dfrac{\partial\Phi}{\partial x} + \Phi\dfrac{\partial u_y}{\partial y} + u_y\dfrac{\partial\Phi}{\partial y} + \Phi\dfrac{\partial u_z}{\partial z} + u_z\dfrac{\partial\Phi}{\partial z}\]Grouping terms:\[= \Phi\underbrace{\left(\dfrac{\partial u_x}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial u_y}{\partial y} + \dfrac{\partial u_z}{\partial z} ight)}_{ ext{div}(\mathbf{u})} + \underbrace{\left(u_x\dfrac{\partial\Phi}{\partial x} + u_y\dfrac{\partial\Phi}{\partial y} + u_z\dfrac{\partial\Phi}{\partial z} ight)}_{\mathbf{u}\cdot ext{grad}(\Phi)}\]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

OptionStatementVerdict
A\(\Phi\, ext{div}(\mathbf{u}) + \mathbf{u}\cdot ext{grad}(\Phi)\)✅ Matches derived identity
BUses cross product \(\mathbf{u} imes ext{grad}(\Phi)\)❌ Yields vector; divergence must be scalar
C\( ext{grad}(\mathbf{u})\) is undefined (gradient of vector = tensor)❌ Not compatible
D\(\Phi\, ext{grad}(\mathbf{u})\) — invalid; cross product also wrong❌ Incorrect

Common Pitfall: Confusing dot product (\(\cdot\)) with cross product (\( imes\)). The divergence of a vector field always yields a scalar, so any term added must also be scalar.

5. Final Answer:

\( ext{div}(\Phi\mathbf{u}) = \Phi\, ext{div}(\mathbf{u}) + \mathbf{u}\cdot ext{grad}(\Phi)\) | Option(s): A

questions.question:
A remote village has exactly 1000 vehicles with sequential registration numbers starting from 1000. Out of the total vehicles, 30% are without pollution clearance certificate. Further, even- and odd-numbered vehicles are operated on even- and odd-numbered dates, respectively.
If 100 vehicles are chosen at random on an even-numbered date, the number of vehicles expected without pollution clearance certificate is _______.
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability & Statistics — Expected Value

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ParameterValue
    Total vehicles1000
    Registration range1000 – 1999
    Pollution non-compliant30%
    Selection dayEven-numbered date
    Sample size100
  • Aim: Expected number of vehicles without pollution clearance certificate in the sample.

2. Core Concepts:

Key Insight: Pollution certificate status is independent of vehicle registration number parity.

Expected Value Formula: \(E[X] = n \times p\), where \(n\) = sample size and \(p\) = probability of no pollution certificate.

Stratified Sampling Principle: When selecting from a subpopulation (even-numbered vehicles), if the characteristic is uniformly distributed, the proportion remains unchanged.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

StepCalculationResult
1Total vehicles1000
2Even-numbered vehicles (1000 to 1998): \(\dfrac{1998-1000}{2}+1\)500
3Non-compliant vehicles overall: \(0.30 \times 1000\)300

6Expected non-compliant in sample of 100: \(100 \times 0.30\)30

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q16
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
When a simply-supported elastic beam of span \( L \) and flexural rigidity \( EI \) (\( E \) is the modulus of elasticity and \( I \) is the moment of inertia of the section) is loaded with a uniformly distributed load \( w \) per unit length, the deflection at the mid-span is \( \Delta_0 = \dfrac{5}{384} \dfrac{wL^4}{EI} \).
If the load on one half of the span is now removed, the mid-span deflection______.
options: reduces to a value less than \( \Delta_0/2 \)
reduces to a value greater than \( \Delta_0/2 \)

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: reduces to a value less than \( \Delta_0/2 \)
structuredOptions.html: reduces to a value less than \( \Delta_0/2 \)

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: reduces to a value greater than \( \Delta_0/2 \)
structuredOptions.html: reduces to a value greater than \( \Delta_0/2 \)

questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Beam Deflections — Superposition Principle

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    ParameterSymbolExpression
    Span\(L\)—
    Flexural rigidity\(EI\)Constant
    Initial UDL\(w\)per unit length over full span
    Initial mid-span deflection\(\Delta_0\)\(\dfrac{5wL^4}{384EI}\)
  • Aim: Find the new mid-span deflection when UDL on one half is removed.

2. Core Concepts:

Superposition Principle: For linear elastic structures, the total deflection due to multiple loads equals the sum of deflections due to each load acting independently.

Symmetry Principle: For a simply supported beam, UDL on the left half produces the same mid-span deflection as an identical UDL on the right half.

3. Solution Method:

Let \(\Delta_{half}\) = mid-span deflection due to UDL on one half only.

By the superposition principle:

\[\Delta_0 = \Delta_{\text{left-half}} + \Delta_{\text{right-half}}\]

By symmetry of the simply-supported beam:

\[\Delta_{\text{left-half}} = \Delta_{\text{right-half}} = \Delta_{half}\]

Therefore:

\[\Delta_0 = 2\Delta_{half} \implies \Delta_{half} = \dfrac{\Delta_0}{2}\]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

StepLogic / CalculationResult
1Initial: Full UDL \(w\) over \(L\)\(\Delta_0 = \dfrac{5wL^4}{384EI}\)
2By symmetry, mid-span deflection due to left-half UDL = mid-span deflection due to right-half UDL\(\Delta_{left} = \Delta_{right}\)
3Superposition: \(\Delta_0 = \Delta_{left} + \Delta_{right} = 2\Delta_{half}\)—

questions.question: A vertical sheet pile wall is installed in an anisotropic soil having coefficient of horizontal permeability, \( k_H \) and coefficient of vertical permeability, \( k_V \). In order to draw the flow net for the isotropic condition, the embedment depth of the wall should be scaled by a factor of _______, without changing the horizontal scale.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage Analysis in Anisotropic Soils

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Horizontal permeability coefficient: \(k_H\)
    • Vertical permeability coefficient: \(k_V\)
    • Horizontal scale: maintained unchanged.
  • Aim: Determine the scaling factor for the vertical dimension (embedment depth) to transform the anisotropic flow domain to an isotropic equivalent for flow net construction.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Anisotropic Flow Transformation: For soils with \(k_H \neq k_V\), coordinate transformation converts the anisotropic domain to an isotropic equivalent:\[x' = x, \quad z' = z \times \sqrt{\dfrac{k_H}{k_V}}\]
  • Governing Equation: The anisotropic Laplace equation:\[k_H \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x^2} + k_V \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial z^2} = 0\]transforms to the isotropic form \(\nabla^2 h = 0\) under the scaling.
  • Equivalent Isotropic Permeability: \(k' = \sqrt{k_H \cdot k_V}\)

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Introduce transformed vertical coordinate: \(z' = z \times \alpha\) where \(\alpha\) is the scaling factor.
  2. Apply chain rule: \(\dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial z^2} = \alpha^2 \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial z'^2}\)
  3. Substitute into governing equation:\[k_H \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x^2} + k_V \alpha^2 \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial z'^2} = 0\]
  4. For isotropic form, require \(k_H = k_V \alpha^2\):\[\alpha^2 = \dfrac{k_H}{k_V} \implies \alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_H}{k_V}}\]

Sanity Check: For typical stratified soils (\(k_H > k_V\)), scaling factor > 1 → vertical dimensions are stretched to compensate for higher horizontal permeability. ✓

4. Final Answer:

Scaling factor = \(\sqrt{\dfrac{k_H}{k_V}}\) | Option(s): A

(D) Variation of soil stiffness along depthWhile stiffness varies with depth (the root cause), the question specifically asks about non-uniformity across the width. (D) is too general and does not directly explain the settlement variation pattern along the width.❌ FALSE (per answer key)

5. Final Answer:

Statement (B) is TRUE | Option(s): B

questions.question: The steady-state temperature distribution in a square plate ABCD is governed by the 2-dimensional Laplace equation. The side AB is kept at a temperature of 100 °C and the other three sides are kept at a temperature of 0 °C. Ignoring the effect of discontinuities in the boundary conditions at the corners, the steady-state temperature at the center of the plate is obtained as \( T_0 \) °C. Due to symmetry, the steady-state temperature at the center will be same (\( T_0 \) °C), when any one side of the square is kept at a temperature of 100 °C and the remaining three sides are kept at a temperature of 0 °C. Using the principle of superposition, the value of \( T_0 \) is _________________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics / Heat Transfer | 2D Steady-State Conduction — Laplace Equation

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Square plate ABCD; side AB at \(100°\)C, other three sides at \(0°\)C; \(T_0\) = temperature at centre.
  • Aim: Find \(T_0\) (°C, two decimal places).

2. Core Concepts:

  • Steady-state temperature satisfies the 2D Laplace equation: \(\nabla^2 T = 0\).
  • Superposition principle applies for linear PDEs.
  • When all four sides are at \(100°\)C, \(T = 100°\)C everywhere (trivial uniform solution).
  • By rotational symmetry, each single-side-hot case contributes equally at the centre.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Consider the case where all four sides are at \(100°\)C:
    \(T(x,y) \equiv 100°\)C everywhere (satisfies Laplace equation and all boundary conditions).
    Centre temperature = \(100°\)C.
  2. By superposition, this is the sum of four individual cases — each with one side at \(100°\)C and the other three at \(0°\)C.
  3. By rotational symmetry of the square plate, each case contributes equally at the centre:\[4 \times T_0 = 100°\text{C}\]
  4. Solving:\[T_0 = \dfrac{100}{4} = 25.00°\text{C}\]

Common Pitfall: Forgetting linearity/symmetry and attempting a full series solution unnecessarily.

4. Final Answer:

\(T_0 = \mathbf{25.00}°\)C | Accepted range: 24.90 to 25.10

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
The solution of the differential equation
\[\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3} - 5.5 \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 9.5 \dfrac{dy}{dx} - 5 y = 0 \]
is expressed as \( y = C_1 e^{2.5x} + C_2 e^{\alpha x} + C_3 e^{\beta x} \), where \( C_1, C_2, C_3, \alpha, \) and \( \beta \) are constants, with \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) being distinct and not equal to 2.5. Which of the following options is correct for the values of \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Solving linear differential equations).
  • Given Equation: \(\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3} - 5.5\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 9.5\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 5y = 0\)
  • Given Solution: \(y = C_1 e^{2.5x} + C_2 e^{\alpha x} + C_3 e^{\beta x}\)
  • Conditions: \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are distinct constants \(\neq 2.5\).
  • Aim: Determine the values of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

2. Core Concepts:

Linear Homogeneous Differential Equation with Constant Coefficients: The general solution is determined by the roots of the auxiliary (characteristic) equation. For an equation \(a_n y^{(n)} + \dots + a_0 y = 0\), the auxiliary equation is \(a_n m^n + \dots + a_0 = 0\).

Solution Form: If roots \(m_1, m_2, m_3\) are distinct real numbers, the solution is \(y = C_1 e^{m_1 x} + C_2 e^{m_2 x} + C_3 e^{m_3 x}\).

3. Solution Method:

  1. Write the auxiliary equation in terms of \(m\).
  2. Use the known root provided in the solution form (\(m = 2.5\)) to factorize the cubic equation.
  3. Solve the remaining quadratic equation to find the other two roots \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formulate the Auxiliary Equation:
    The differential equation is: \(D^3 - 5.5D^2 + 9.5D - 5 = 0\) where \(D = \dfrac{d}{dx}\).
    The auxiliary equation is:\[m^3 - 5.5m^2 + 9.5m - 5 = 0\]
  2. Use the Known Root:
    Since \(e^{2.5x}\) is part of the solution, \(m = 2.5\) is a root. Perform synthetic division with coefficients \([1,\ -5.5,\ 9.5,\ -5]\) and \(m = 2.5\):
    • Bring down \(1\).
    • \(1 \times 2.5 = 2.5\). Add: \(-5.5 + 2.5 = -3.0\).
    • \(-3.0 \times 2.5 = -7.5\). Add: \(9.5 - 7.5 = 2.0\).
    • \(2.0 \times 2.5 = 5.0\). Add: \(-5 + 5 = 0\). (Remainder = 0, confirmed).
    The resulting quadratic equation is:\[m^2 - 3m + 2 = 0\]
  3. Solve for Remaining Roots:
    Factorize:\[m^2 - 2m - m + 2 = 0\]\[m(m-2) - 1(m-2) = 0\]\[(m-1)(m-2) = 0\]
    The roots are \(m = 1\) and \(m = 2\), corresponding to \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

5. Final Answer:

The values are 1 and 2 | Option(s): A

questions.question: Two vectors \( [2 \quad 1 \quad 0 \quad 3]^T \) and \( [1 \quad 0 \quad 1 \quad 2]^T \) belong to the null space of a \( 4 \times 4 \) matrix of rank 2. Which one of the following vectors also belongs to the null space?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Vector spaces, Rank, Null Space).
  • Given Data:
    • Matrix size: \(4 imes 4\).
    • Rank of Matrix \(r = 2\).
    • Vectors in Null Space: \(v_1 = [2,\ 1,\ 0,\ 3]^T\) and \(v_2 = [1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2]^T\).
  • Aim: Identify which option vector also belongs to the null space.

2. Core Concepts:

Rank-Nullity Theorem:\[ ext{Rank} + ext{Nullity} = ext{Number of Columns}\]\[2 + ext{Nullity} = 4 \implies ext{Nullity} = 2\]

Null Space Basis: Since the nullity is 2, the null space has dimension 2. The two given linearly independent vectors \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) form a basis for the null space.

Linear Combination: Any vector \(w\) in the null space must satisfy:\[w = c_1 v_1 + c_2 v_2\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Express the unknown vector \(w = [w_1,\ w_2,\ w_3,\ w_4]^T\) as \(c_1 v_1 + c_2 v_2\).
  2. Set up the system of linear equations for each component.
  3. Test each option to see if consistent values for \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) exist.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Let the target vector be \(w\):

\[w = c_1 egin{bmatrix} 2 \ 1 \ 0 \ 3 \end{bmatrix} + c_2 egin{bmatrix} 1 \ 0 \ 1 \ 2 \end{bmatrix} = egin{bmatrix} 2c_1 + c_2 \ c_1 \ c_2 \ 3c_1 + 2c_2 \end{bmatrix}\]

From rows 2 and 3, for any candidate vector \([x,\ y,\ z,\ k]^T\): \(y = c_1\) and \(z = c_2\).
Verification conditions:

  • Condition 1: \(x = 2y + z\)
  • Condition 2: \(k = 3y + 2z\)

Test Option (A): \([1,\ 1,\ -1,\ 1]^T\) — \(y=1,\ z=-1\)
Check \(x\): \(2(1)+(-1)=1\) ✓
Check \(k\): \(3(1)+2(-1)=1\) ✓ Valid.

Test Option (B): \([2,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2]^T\) — \(y=0,\ z=1\)
Check \(x\): \(2(0)+1=1 eq 2\) ✗

Test Option (C): \([0,\ -2,\ 1,\ -1]^T\) — \(y=-2,\ z=1\)
Check \(x\): \(2(-2)+1=-3 eq 0\) ✗

Test Option (D): \([3,\ 1,\ 1,\ 2]^T\) — \(y=1,\ z=1\)
Check \(x\): \(2(1)+1=3\) ✓
Check \(k\): \(3(1)+2(1)=5 eq 2\) ✗

5. Final Answer:

The vector \([1,\ 1,\ -1,\ 1]^T\) belongs to the null space. | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Cholesky decomposition is carried out on the following square matrix \( [A] \).
\[ [A] = \begin{bmatrix} 8 & -5 \\ -5 & a_{22} \end{bmatrix} \]
Let \( l_{ij} \) and \( a_{ij} \) be the (i,j)th elements of matrices \( [L] \) and \( [A] \), respectively. If the element \( l_{22} \) of the decomposed lower triangular matrix \( [L] \) is 1.968, what is the value (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the element \( a_{22} \)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Matrix Decomposition).
  • Topic: Cholesky Decomposition (\(A = LL^T\)).
  • Given Data:
    • Matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 8 & -5 \\ -5 & a_{22} \end{bmatrix}\)
    • \(l_{22} = 1.968\)
  • Aim: Find \(a_{22}\) rounded to the nearest integer.

2. Core Concepts:

Cholesky Decomposition: For a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(A\), \(A = LL^T\), where \(L\) is a lower triangular matrix:

\[L = \begin{bmatrix} l_{11} & 0 \\ l_{21} & l_{22} \end{bmatrix}\]\[LL^T = \begin{bmatrix} l_{11} & 0 \\ l_{21} & l_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} l_{11} & l_{21} \\ 0 & l_{22} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} l_{11}^2 & l_{11}l_{21} \\ l_{11}l_{21} & l_{21}^2 + l_{22}^2 \end{bmatrix}\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Equate elements of \(A\) to the elements of \(LL^T\).
  2. Solve for \(l_{11}\), then \(l_{21}\).
  3. Use \(l_{21}\) and the given \(l_{22}\) to find \(a_{22}\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Equate element \(A_{11}\):\[l_{11}^2 = 8 \implies l_{11} = \sqrt{8}\]
  2. Equate element \(A_{21}\):\[l_{11} l_{21} = -5\]\[\sqrt{8} \cdot l_{21} = -5 \implies l_{21} = \dfrac{-5}{\sqrt{8}}\]
  3. Equate element \(A_{22}\):\[a_{22} = l_{21}^2 + l_{22}^2\]\[a_{22} = \left(\dfrac{-5}{\sqrt{8}}\right)^2 + (1.968)^2\]\[a_{22} = \dfrac{25}{8} + 3.873024\]\[a_{22} = 3.125 + 3.873024 = 6.998024\]
  4. Rounding: Round to the nearest integer: \(a_{22} \approx 7\).

5. Final Answer:

The value of \(a_{22}\) is 7 | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: In a two-dimensional stress analysis, the state of stress at a point is shown in the figure. The values of length of PQ, QR, and RP are 4, 3, and 5 units, respectively. The principal stresses are _______. (round off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Principal Stresses

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Stress Transformation).
  • Given Data:
    • Geometry: Triangular element PQR with sides PQ = 4, QR = 3, RP = 5.
    • Stresses on Inclined Plane RP: Normal Stress \(\sigma_n = 120\) MPa (Tensile), Shear Stress \(\tau_{nt} = 70\) MPa.
    • Stresses on Faces PQ and QR: Only normal stresses (\(\sigma_x\) on vertical face PQ, \(\sigma_y\) on horizontal face QR).
  • Crucial Inference: Since no shear stress arrows are drawn on faces PQ and QR, \(\tau_{xy} = 0\). Thus, \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\) are the principal stresses.
  • Aim: Find the principal stresses \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\).

2. Core Concepts:

Stress Transformation Equations (for Principal Planes, \(\tau_{xy} = 0\)):
For a plane whose normal makes an angle \(\theta\) with the x-axis:

\[\sigma_n = \sigma_x \cos^2\theta + \sigma_y \sin^2\theta\]\[\tau_{nt} = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)\sin\theta\cos\theta\]

Note: Sign convention for shear may vary, but magnitude is absolute.

Geometry: The inclined face RP connects points \((0,4)\) and \((3,0)\) (assuming local origin at Q).
Normal Vector \(\vec{n} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\).
Angle \(\theta\) of normal with x-axis:

\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3^2+4^2}} = \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8\]\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute \(\theta\), \(\sigma_n\), and \(\tau_{nt}\) into the transformation equations.
  2. Solve the system of two linear equations for \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Shear Stress Equation:\[\tau_{nt} = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)\sin\theta\cos\theta\]\[70 = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)(0.6)(0.8)\]\[70 = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)(0.48)\]\[\sigma_y - \sigma_x = \dfrac{70}{0.48} = 145.833 \text{ MPa} \quad \cdots(1)\]
  2. Normal Stress Equation:\[\sigma_n = \sigma_x\cos^2\theta + \sigma_y\sin^2\theta\]\[120 = \sigma_x(0.8)^2 + \sigma_y(0.6)^2\]\[120 = 0.64\sigma_x + 0.36\sigma_y \quad \cdots(2)\]
  3. Solve Simultaneous Equations:
    From (1): \(\sigma_y = \sigma_x + 145.833\). Substitute into (2):\[120 = 0.64\sigma_x + 0.36(\sigma_x + 145.833)\]\[120 = 0.64\sigma_x + 0.36\sigma_x + 52.5\]\[120 = \sigma_x + 52.5\]\[\sigma_x = 67.5 \text{ MPa}\]
    Find \(\sigma_y\):\[\sigma_y = 67.5 + 145.833 = 213.33 \text{ MPa}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(\sigma_x = 67.5\) MPa, \(\sigma_y = 213.3\) MPa | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: Two plates are connected by fillet welds of size 10 mm and subjected to tension, as shown in the figure. The thickness of each plate is 12 mm. The yield stress and the ultimate stress of steel under tension are 250 MPa and 410 MPa, respectively. The welding is done in the workshop (partial safety factor, \( \gamma_{mw} = 1.25 \)). As per the Limit State Method of IS 800: 2007, what is the minimum length (in mm, rounded off to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm) required of each weld to transmit a factored force \( P \) equal to 275 kN?
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Welded Connections

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Design of Fillet Weld).
  • Code: IS 800:2007 (Limit State Method).
  • Given Data:
    • Factored Load \(P = 275\) kN.
    • Weld Size \(S = 10\) mm.
    • Partial Safety Factor \(\gamma_{mw} = 1.25\) (Workshop weld).
    • Material: \(f_u = 410\) MPa.
    • Configuration: Two plates connected by two longitudinal fillet welds (top and bottom).
  • Aim: Find the minimum length of each weld (rounded to higher multiple of 5 mm).

2. Core Concepts:

Design Strength of Fillet Weld (\(P_{dw}\)):\[P_{dw} = L_w \times t_t \times f_{wd}\]\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{f_u}{\sqrt{3}\, \gamma_{mw}}\]

Throat Thickness (\(t_t\)): For \(90^\circ\) fusion faces, \(t_t = 0.7 \times S\).

Load Sharing: Since there are two welds, each weld carries \(P/2\), or total capacity = \(2 \times\) individual capacity.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Design Stress (\(f_{wd}\)):\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{410}{\sqrt{3} \times 1.25} = \dfrac{410}{2.165} = 189.37 \text{ N/mm}^2\]
  2. Calculate Throat Thickness (\(t_t\)):\[t_t = 0.7 \times 10 = 7 \text{ mm}\]
  3. Calculate Required Effective Length (\(L_{eff}\)):
    Total Load Capacity required = \(275\) kN = \(275 \times 10^3\) N.

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In the given figure, Point O indicates the stress point of a soil element at initial non-hydrostatic stress condition. For the stress path (OP), which of the following loading conditions is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics — Stress Path

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Initial stress condition at Point O.
    • Stress path (OP) drawn in the \(p\)-\(q\) space.
    • The slope of line OP is given graphically as \(1\) (vertical leg \(= 1\), horizontal leg \(= 1\)).
  • Aim: Determine the correct loading condition (variation of vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) and horizontal stress \(\sigma_h\)) that corresponds to the given stress path.

2. Core Concepts:

Stress Invariants:

  • Mean effective stress: \(p = \dfrac{\sigma_v + \sigma_h}{2}\)
  • Deviatoric stress: \(q = \dfrac{\sigma_v - \sigma_h}{2}\)

Stress Path Slope: The slope of the \(p\)-\(q\) plot is defined as \(m = \dfrac{\Delta q}{\Delta p}\).

3. Solution Method:

By evaluating the mathematical slope of the given stress path, we can establish a relationship between \(\Delta\sigma_v\) and \(\Delta\sigma_h\). Applying the graphical direction (upward and rightward) will tell us whether the stresses are increasing or decreasing.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine the slope from the graph:
    The right-angled triangle on the stress path OP shows a rise of \(1\) and a run of \(1\).\[\text{Slope} = \dfrac{\Delta q}{\Delta p} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1\]
  2. Substitute \(p\) and \(q\) variations:\[\Delta q = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v - \Delta\sigma_h}{2}, \quad \Delta p = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v + \Delta\sigma_h}{2}\]
  3. Equate and solve for stress changes:\[\dfrac{\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v - \Delta\sigma_h}{2}}{\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v + \Delta\sigma_h}{2}} = 1\]\[\Delta\sigma_v - \Delta\sigma_h = \Delta\sigma_v + \Delta\sigma_h\]
    Subtract \(\Delta\sigma_v\) from both sides:\[-\Delta\sigma_h = \Delta\sigma_h\]\[2\Delta\sigma_h = 0 \implies \Delta\sigma_h = 0\]
    This means the horizontal stress \(\sigma_h\) is constant.
  4. Determine the direction of vertical stress:
    The path OP moves upwards, meaning \(q\) is increasing (\(\Delta q > 0\)).\[\Delta q = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v - 0}{2} > 0 \implies \Delta\sigma_v > 0\]
    This means the vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) is increasing.

5. Final Answer:

\(\sigma_v\) is increasing and \(\sigma_h\) is constant | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q42

questions.question: The figure shows a vertical retaining wall with backfill consisting of cohesive-frictional soil and a failure plane developed due to passive earth pressure. The forces acting on the failure wedge are: \( P \) as the reaction force between the wall and the soil, \( R \) as the reaction force on the failure plane, \( C \) as the cohesive force along the failure plane and \( W \) as the weight of the failure wedge. Assuming that there is no adhesion between the wall and the wedge, identify the most appropriate force polygon for the wedge.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theory

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Vertical retaining wall retaining cohesive-frictional soil.
    • Failure plane developed due to passive earth pressure.
    • No adhesion between the wall and the wedge.
    • Forces: \(P\) (reaction from wall), \(R\) (reaction from soil), \(C\) (cohesive force), \(W\) (weight).
  • Aim: Identify the most appropriate, mathematically closed force polygon for the failure wedge.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Passive State Kinematics: The wall is pushed into the soil backfill. The failure soil wedge is consequently pushed upward and outward along the inclined failure plane.
  • Force Equilibrium (\(\sum \vec{F} = 0\)): The vectors must form a closed polygon when placed tip-to-tail.
  • Direction of Resistance: Frictional and cohesive forces always act in the direction opposite to the relative impending motion.

3. Solution Method:

Map out the true physical directions of all 4 forces acting on the wedge, then trace the vector additions to see which polygon structurally matches.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Vector Directions:
    • Weight (\(W\)): Gravity acts vertically downward (↓).
    • Cohesion (\(C\)): The wedge is moving up the failure plane. Cohesion resists this, so it acts downward along the failure plane (↙).
    • Failure plane reaction (\(R\)): The stationary soil resists the wedge's sliding via friction, so \(R\) points upward and to the left (↖).
    • Wall reaction (\(P\)): The wall pushes the wedge to the right; since the wedge moves upward relative to the wall, wall friction acts downward on the wedge. Thus \(P\) pushes to the right and slightly downward (↘).
  2. Evaluate the Polygons:
    Trace the correct sequence starting with \(W\):
    • \(W\) goes ↓
    • From \(W\)'s tip, \(C\) goes ↙
    • From \(C\)'s tip, \(R\) goes ↖
    • From \(R\)'s tip, \(P\) must close the shape going ↘ or → to reach \(W\)'s tail.
    Option (A): Vector \(P\) slopes upward (↗) — implies wall friction acting upward, which only occurs in the active state. (Incorrect)
    Option (B): Vector placement does not form a sequential physical polygon. (Incorrect)
    Option (C): \(W\) goes ↓, \(C\) goes ↙, \(R\) goes ↖, and \(P\) closes the loop pointing ↘. This perfectly matches passive state mechanics. (Correct)

5. Final Answer:

The polygon with \(W\) ↓, \(C\) ↙, \(R\) ↖, \(P\) ↘ | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A compound symmetrical open channel section as shown in the figure has a maximum of _________ critical depth(s).
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow — Compound Channels

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: A standard symmetrical compound open channel section.
  • Aim: Identify the maximum possible number of critical depths such a channel can experience.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Specific Energy: \(E = y + \dfrac{\alpha Q^2}{2g A^2}\)
  • Froude Number: \(F^2 = \dfrac{\alpha Q^2 T}{g A^3}\). Critical flow occurs when \(F = 1\).
  • Hydraulic behaviour in compound channels: When water level just spills over the main channel banks into the flood plains, there is a sudden and massive jump in the top width (\(T\)), while the flow area (\(A\)) continues to increase gradually.

3. Solution Method:

Analyze the physical behavior of the specific energy curve and Froude number variations as depth \(y\) increases from the main channel into the flood plains.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Flow contained in main channel (\(y < y_m\)): The channel behaves like a simple rectangular section. It yields one potential critical depth where \(E\) is minimal.
  2. Water overtopping the bank (\(y \ge y_m\)): The top width \(T\) abruptly increases from \(B_m\) to \((B_m + 2B_f)\). Since \(T\) is in the numerator of the Froude number equation, \(F\) spikes sharply. A flow that was subcritical (\(F < 1\)) inside the main channel can suddenly become supercritical (\(F > 1\)) just over the flood plain.
  3. Flow rising further in the floodplain: As depth increases further, the wetted area \(A\) grows. The \(A^3\) term in the denominator overtakes the constant wide \(T\), driving \(F\) back below 1. This crossing provides another critical flow state.
  4. Conclusion: Because the \(E\)-\(y\) curve takes a localized zig-zag (or "S") shape due to the flood plains, it can possess up to three local extremes — giving a maximum of 3 critical depths.

5. Final Answer:

Maximum number of critical depths = 3 | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
The critical flow condition in a channel is given by _________.
[Note: \( \alpha \) – kinetic energy correction factor; \( Q \) – discharge; \( A_c \) – cross-sectional area of flow at critical flow condition; \( T_c \) – top width of flow at critical flow condition; \( g \) – acceleration due to gravity]
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow — Critical Flow

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: Variables \(\alpha,\ Q,\ A_c,\ T_c,\ g\).
  • Aim: Derive or identify the exact analytical condition for critical flow in an open channel.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Specific Energy equation: \(E = y + \dfrac{\alpha Q^2}{2g A^2}\)
  • Calculus of Critical Flow: Critical depth occurs at the state of minimum specific energy for a constant discharge \(Q\). Therefore, \(\dfrac{dE}{dy} = 0\).

3. Solution Method:

Differentiate the specific energy equation with respect to depth \(y\) and set the equation to zero to solve for the critical state relation.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Differentiate Specific Energy:\[\dfrac{dE}{dy} = \dfrac{d}{dy}\left[y + \dfrac{\alpha Q^2}{2g}\left(A^{-2}\right)\right]\]
  2. Apply the chain rule:\[\dfrac{dE}{dy} = 1 + \left(\dfrac{\alpha Q^2}{2g}\right)\left(-2A^{-3}\right)\dfrac{dA}{dy}\]
  3. Relate Area and Depth: The infinitesimal change in area with respect to depth is the top width \(T\).\[\dfrac{dA}{dy} = T_c\]
  4. Equate to Zero: Set the derivative to zero and substitute \(T_c\):\[1 - \dfrac{\alpha Q^2 \cdot T_c}{g A_c^3} = 0\]
  5. Rearrange:\[\dfrac{\alpha Q^2}{g} = \dfrac{A_c^3}{T_c}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(\dfrac{\alpha Q^2}{g} = \dfrac{A_c^3}{T_c}\) | Option(s): A

The direction of each path is given in the table below as whole circle bearings. Assume that the latitude (L) and departure (D) of R is (0, 0) km. What is the latitude and departure of P (in km, rounded off to one decimal place)?

PathsRCCAABBP

questions.explanation:
Geomatics Engineering | Traverse Surveying

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Starting Coordinates of R: \(L_R = 0.0\text{ km},\ D_R = 0.0\text{ km}\)
    • Length of each path (\(l\)): \(5\text{ km}\)
    • Whole Circle Bearings (WCB, \(\theta\)): RC = \(120^\circ\), CA = \(0^\circ\), AB = \(90^\circ\), BP = \(240^\circ\)
  • Aim: Calculate the final Latitude (\(L\)) and Departure (\(D\)) of point P.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Latitude (\(L\)): The orthographic projection of a survey line on the North–South axis.\[L = l\cos\theta\](Positive towards North, Negative towards South)
  • Departure (\(D\)): The orthographic projection of a survey line on the East–West axis.\[D = l\sin\theta\](Positive towards East, Negative towards West)
  • Principle of Superposition:\[L_P = L_R + \sum L \quad;\quad D_P = D_R + \sum D\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the individual latitude and departure for each of the four segments (RC, CA, AB, BP).
  2. Algebraically sum the latitudes and departures.
  3. Add sums to the initial coordinates of R to get coordinates of P.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Calculate Latitude and Departure for each leg

LineBearing (\(\theta\))Latitude \(= 5\cos\theta\) (km)Departure \(= 5\sin\theta\) (km)
RC\(120^\circ\)\(5 \times (-0.5) = -2.5\)\(5 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = +4.330\)
CA\(0^\circ\)\(5 \times 1 = +5.0\)\(5 \times 0 = 0.0\)
AB\(90^\circ\)\(5 \times 0 = 0.0\)\(5 \times 1 = +5.0\)
BP\(240^\circ\)\(5 \times (-0.5) = -2.5\)\(5 \times \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -4.330\)

Step 2: Sum the Latitudes and Departures

\[\sum L = -2.5 + 5.0 + 0.0 - 2.5 = 0.0\text{ km}\]\[\sum D = +4.330 + 0.0 + 5.0 - 4.330 = +5.0\text{ km}\]

Step 3: Calculate Final Coordinates

\[L_P = L_R + \sum L = 0.0 + 0.0 = 0.0\text{ km}\]\[D_P = D_R + \sum D = 0.0 + 5.0 = +5.0\text{ km}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(L = 0.0\text{ km},\ D = 5.0\text{ km}\) | Option(s): B

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Analysis
  • Given Data: Four theoretical statements regarding boundary layer theory, kinematics, fluid statics, and pipe flow.
  • Aim: Identify the TRUE statement(s) among the given options (Multiple Select Question).

2. Core Concepts & Solution Method:

Statement (A): Thickness of turbulent boundary layer (\(\delta\))
For a flat plate parallel to the flow, the boundary layer thickness grows as:

  • Laminar flow: \(\delta \propto x^{1/2}\) (Blasius solution)
  • Turbulent flow: \(\delta \propto x^{4/5}\) (i.e., \(x^{0.8}\)), derived from the 1/7th power velocity law.

The statement claims turbulent thickness is proportional to \(x^{1/2}\). This is incorrect. (FALSE)

Statement (B): Interchange of streamlines and equipotential lines of a source
For a 2D source, streamlines are radial straight lines and equipotential lines are concentric circles. If interchanged, streamlines become concentric circles — representing a Free Vortex, not a sink. (FALSE)

Statement (C): Vertical force on a curved surface
The vertical component of hydrostatic force equals the weight of the fluid volume physically or virtually enclosed above the curved surface up to the free surface. This is a direct statement of fundamental fluid statics. (TRUE)

Statement (D): Momentum correction factor (\(\beta\))
\[\beta = \dfrac{1}{A V_{avg}^2}\int u^2\, dA\]

  • Laminar flow (parabolic profile): \(\beta = \dfrac{4}{3} \approx 1.33\)
  • Turbulent flow (flat profile): \(\beta \approx 1.01\) to \(1.05\)
Since \(1.33 > 1.05\), \(\beta\) for laminar flow is indeed larger than for turbulent flow. (TRUE)

3. Final Answer:

Statements (C) and (D) are true | Option(s): C, D

2. Core Concepts:

In a time-space diagram (Distance on Y-axis, Time on X-axis):

  • Speed (\(v\)): Represented by the slope of the trajectory. Steeper slope = Higher speed. Horizontal line = Zero speed.
  • Density (\(k\)): Inversely proportional to the vertical spacing between trajectories (distance headway).
  • Volume/Flow (\(q\)): Inversely proportional to horizontal spacing (time headway). Governed by the fundamental equation \(q = k \times v\).

RegionSpeedVolumeDensity

R (Discharge)\(v_R\) = optimum speed; \(v_P > v_R\)\(q_R = q_{max}\) (capacity); \(q_R > q_P\)\(k_R = k_c\) (optimum density; \(k_c < k_j\))

  • (C) Volume is higher in Region R than in Region P: Region R is at capacity flow (\(q_{max}\)). For the queue to dissipate, discharge rate must exceed the approach volume: \(q_R > q_P\). (TRUE)
